_comment: 'parameters' is the base customizer parameter set applied to every fan. Each entry
in 'sizes' is rendered once, with its own 'parameters' merged on top of the base.
Anything the script computes from its arguments (Blade_Cutout_SVG_File,
Blade_Cutout_SVG_Scale, Rendering_Mode) overrides both - editing those here has no
effect. Every other parameter of the .scad falls back to the default in the file.
Values are strings, matching the format OpenSCAD writes into its own
_outputs_comment: default_outputs is what a plain run produces; --resulting-files overrides it.
Valid entries: stl, 3mf, colored, assembled, png.
colored and assembled are the same fan with the etch layer black, so the artwork
reads instead of sitting white on a white blade. They differ only in layout:
colored is the printing layout, the file that gets sliced; assembled is the fan as
it ends up in the hand, the view the picture shows.
Both go out as 3MF because that is the format that carries colour. An STL would be
one merged solid with the black thrown away - identical to the plain STL.
Each block takes its own rendering_mode, extension, suffix and parameters, so a
new variant is a new block plus its name in default_outputs.
_export_3mf_comment: Passed to OpenSCAD as -O export-3mf/<key>=<value> on every 3MF written. The CLI
does not read the GUI's export preferences, and its own default for material-type
is basematerial - a form many slicers and viewers ignore, so the file opens as one
flat colour even though the colours are in it. "color" writes a colorgroup, which
is what they read. Run 'OpenSCAD --help-export' for the full list of keys.
_colored_comment: White everywhere except the etching, which is black and confined to the artwork
itself - Etch_Layer_Extent=artwork keeps the second colour under the etched shapes
instead of flooding the whole blade at that depth. The colours are pinned here
rather than inherited so this file stays white-and-black even if the fan's own
colours change. Etch_Layer_Extent and Hardware_Color need Hand Fan Generator v3.
_models_comment: stl_format is passed to OpenSCAD as --export-format. "binstl" keeps these files
manageable - the same fan is about 180 MB as OpenSCAD's default ASCII STL and
roughly 35 MB as binary. Set it to "" to go back to ASCII.
Each format is exported by its own OpenSCAD call, because --export-format applies
_image_comment: camera is OpenSCAD's gimbal form: translate_x,y,z,rot_x,y,z,distance.
rot_x = 20 looks down on the spread fan at a slight angle - straight down (0)
renders the faces flat on and loses the etched artwork, and the standard 55 deg
3/4 view foreshortens the sector too much to judge the design. distance is left
at 0 because view_all recomputes it, which is what keeps one camera usable for
render:true is worth keeping. An SVG-cut fan is 15 blades of dense geometry, and
OpenSCAD's default PNG path (OpenCSG preview) spends over 12 minutes on it and
still speckles where the etch layer meets the blade face. A full geometry pass
takes about a minute and comes out clean.
image.parameters is merged in last, for the ones that only make sense in a picture.
The etch layer is white on a white blade on the printed fan, which is the point of
it, but in a render that reads as a blank fan - black is what makes the artwork show.
models.parameters does the same for the printed files and is empty by default.
